analysis.investment_thesis: Hemisphere Properties is uninvestable under the Magic Formula — negative EBIT for all four years means both Earnings Yield and ROIC cannot be computed meaningfully. With INR 1 Cr in annual revenue against a INR 3,773 Cr market cap, this is a speculative land-bank bet, not a business.
key_strengths: Asset backing: INR 1,102 Cr in total assets (primarily land) vs INR 60 Cr debt — balance sheet is not leveraged
Manageable debt: D/E of 0.20 with finance costs stable at ~INR 6 Cr/year, no near-term solvency risk
Promoter skin in game: 51.12% promoter holding indicates alignment, though this hasn't produced earnings
key_risks: Magic Formula is inapplicable: EBIT is negative every single year (-3 to -15 Cr), making both Earnings Yield and ROIC meaningless or negative
Obscene valuation relative to earnings: P/S of 3,866x and EV/EBITDA of -385.9x — entirely speculative pricing with zero operational justification
Structural cash burn: OCF negative all 4 years (0/4 positive), Free Cash Flow never positive, suggesting the land bank cannot self-fund and may require ongoing dilution or debt
red_flags: EBIT negative all 4 years: 2022: -13 Cr, 2023: -1 Cr, 2024: -6 Cr, 2025: -3 Cr — no earnings yield computable
Revenue of INR 1 Cr against market cap of INR 3,773 Cr — P/S of 3,866x is not a typo, it's a warning
Operating Margin of -938.1% — costs dwarf revenue by nearly 10x
OCF negative every year: 2022: -14, 2023: -23, 2024: -7, 2025: -17 Cr — this company consumes cash, it does not generate it
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Magic Formula standpoint, Hemisphere Properties is a non-starter. The formula requires positive EBIT to rank on Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) and Return on Capital (EBIT / Net Working Capital + Fixed Assets). EBIT has been negative every year from 2022–2025, ranging from -1 Cr to -13 Cr. There is simply no "E" to calculate. The stock is priced at 3,866x sales — which itself is just INR 1 Cr annually — implying the market is paying for land optionality, not business performance. That is the antithesis of the Magic Formula approach.

The balance sheet tells the only semi-coherent story: INR 1,102 Cr in assets (largely land) against only INR 60 Cr in debt. But market cap of INR 3,773 Cr already prices this land at a 3.4x premium to book, with no evidence the company can develop or monetize it profitably. ROCE is -0.80%, ROE is -1.89%, and operating cash flow has been negative every year. A company that cannot earn returns on its capital, generates almost no revenue, and burns cash structurally deserves the lowest possible score under any value-investing framework — but especially under the Magic Formula which demands both cheapness AND quality of returns.
